themes.name: chain_not_connected
themes.description: A step's end node is not the next step's subject, so chains break into fragments, parallel arms or stars, and genes have no route to the disease (or reach it only by borrowing another hypothesis's steps or a bridge).

themes.name: chain_ends_at_phenotype
themes.description: The chain stops at a phenotype, endophenotype or process (e.g. motor neuron degeneration, plaque compaction) and never reaches the disease itself.

themes.name: database_record_as_causal_evidence
themes.description: Enrichment results (Reactome/STRING/GO over-representation), STRING edges, Open Targets scores, HPA expression, bare UniProt/ChEMBL/trial/AGR model records are cited as if they stated a directed causal step.

themes.name: literature_does_not_state_step
themes.description: Steps are uncited, or cite papers that do not name the step's entities, report a disease feature rather than a cause, or are stitched from two findings neither of which states the link.

themes.name: gwas_row_misused
themes.description: GWAS rows are cited for mechanism steps they cannot state, lack a named risk allele, map to a gene only by position, are for proxy or cross-disorder traits, and no variant-to-gene step exists to carry them.

themes.name: sign_asserted_without_evidence
themes.description: A step is given a direction (e.g. risk allele lowers the gene, loss of function, decreases) that no cited text supports, often read from undirected MGI 'abnormal' annotations or allele names.

themes.name: direction_omitted_or_hedged
themes.description: Steps or claims are left unsigned, hedged, or point at 'abnormal' nodes even when the run's own mechanism or cited text gives a direction.

themes.name: sign_contradicts_source_or_run
themes.description: A step's sign is opposite to its cited text, its own note, or another hypothesis in the same run, so composed routes contradict the claimed direction.

themes.name: supporting_citation_at_no_step
themes.description: Citations listed as supporting evidence are attached to no chain step and state none, so they pad the evidence list without carrying weight.

themes.name: stated_link_unused_or_misplaced
themes.description: The run holds text that directly states a useful link (often its strongest evidence) but cites it at the wrong step or makes no step from it.

themes.name: confidence_mislabelled
themes.description: The confidence/support label ('high', 'grounded', or 'low/speculative') does not match the chain's connectivity and the evidence that actually states its steps.

themes.name: own_contradicting_evidence_ignored
themes.description: Text the run itself cites undercuts the hypothesis (opposite direction, null, conflicting allele effects or source conflicts) and the hypothesis never acknowledges or reconciles it.

themes.name: contradicting_list_malformed
themes.description: The contradicting_evidence list is empty, prose without accessions, not in sources.json, listed both ways, misread, or holds citations that actually support the hypothesis or bear on no step.

themes.name: node_label_and_typing
themes.description: Nodes have empty or malformed CURIEs (e.g. 'EFO:MONDO_...'), vague, compound or pathway-name labels, wrong kinds, or misused relations and schema slots.

themes.name: mechanism_prose_factual_error
themes.description: Mechanism text makes uncited or overstated claims, mischaracterises a source, or uses the wrong entity/accession (wrong HPA record, paralogue or mouse numbering, malformed PMID, copied typo).

themes.name: context_scope_mismatch
themes.description: A step's tissue, cell type, species, disease or trait scope is not what the cited evidence tested (mouse/zebrafish, other cell types, broader disease, severity vs risk).

themes.name: gene_coverage_gaps
themes.description: Question genes get no hypothesis, appear only in titles or qualifiers but no step, or the run returns fewer hypotheses than the budget requires.

themes.name: abstention_unsupported
themes.description: Abstentions set genes aside against the run's own evidence (e.g. IFNW1 and interferon enrichment), overgeneralise from a few nulls, or cite records not in sources.json so they cannot be checked.

themes.name: restates_published_finding
themes.description: The hypothesis and its falsification test restate a retrieved paper's title and already-reported experiment rather than proposing something new.

themes.name: other
themes.description: One-offs: falsification fields inconsistent or incomplete, hand-added hypotheses, rival-claim handling, and lexical evidence sampling.

themes.name: gene_level_record_cited_for_mechanism_step
themes.description: GWAS rows, Open Targets scores, MGI gene phenotypes and ChEMBL/trial records, which only tie a gene or variant to the disease, are cited for process or mechanism steps (often the terminal process-to-disease step) that they cannot state.

themes.name: expression_interaction_enrichment_as_causal_evidence
themes.description: CELLxGENE/HPA detection rates, text-mined STRING edges and STRING/Reactome over-representation results on the input gene list are cited as evidence for directed causal, binding or activation steps, which they cannot carry (and are sometimes misread or circular).

themes.name: cited_text_does_not_state_step
themes.description: Papers and UniProt entries cited at a step are about something else (another entity, disease, readout or relation), are hedged, or state a weaker or different relation than the step claims.

themes.name: evidence_attached_to_no_step
themes.description: Supporting citations, including the run's strongest signed GWAS rows, sit at no step, at the wrong step, or state a link no step makes (often because no variant-to-gene step exists), so they support nothing.

themes.name: chain_not_connected
themes.description: Consecutive steps share no node (fragments, stars, forks, restarts at a new gene, gene only in a label, or chain ends at a phenotype), so some genes have no route to the disease.

themes.name: steps_left_unsigned
themes.description: Steps use polarity 'unknown', 'binds' or 'associated_with' even where the label, note, mechanism or cited text gives a direction, so no gene composes a signed route to the disease.

themes.name: chain_sign_contradicts_mechanism
themes.description: The signs written in the chain compose to the opposite of (or an undetermined version of) the direction the mechanism asserts, e.g. loss-of-function polarity on a bare gene subject or 'dysregulation' signed as a quantity.

themes.name: mechanism_or_title_not_in_chain
themes.description: The mechanism or title names intermediates (cited mediators, specific isoforms, phagocytosis, compaction, glycosylated IgA1) that the chain skips, coarsens or replaces with template steps.

themes.name: node_grounding_kind_and_context
themes.description: Chain nodes have empty or wrong CURIEs, wrong kinds or relations, compound or vague labels, markers used as actors, or boilerplate/misplaced cell-type contexts.

themes.name: confidence_or_support_overstated
themes.description: Confidence 'high'/'medium' or support 'grounded' is assigned to hypotheses whose steps have no stating evidence, broken chains, or self-contradicting self-assessments.

themes.name: contradicting_evidence_missing_ignored_or_misfiled
themes.description: Contradicting-evidence lists are empty, or the run ignores its own citations that state the opposite, cites only the convenient half of a text, or files citations as contradicting/supporting inconsistently.

themes.name: variant_allele_and_locus_handling
themes.description: GWAS variants are assigned to the wrong or a single gene at multi-gene loci, alleles and their effect direction are unknown or ignored, variant function (gain/loss) is never stated, traits are proxies, and inconsistent GWAS rows are taken at face value.

themes.name: falsification_test_mismatched
themes.description: Falsification tests are unstructured, test the wrong aspect, step or gene set, propose infeasible or already-reported experiments, or give expected directions that conflict with the chain.

themes.name: abstention_and_unexplained_genes
themes.description: Abstentions cite evidence ids absent from sources.json so they cannot be checked, and some input genes are left unexplained or listed inconsistently (e.g. used in a mechanism yet listed unexplained, or listed explained with an empty chain).

themes.name: aspect_mismatch_risk_vs_progression
themes.description: Mechanisms claim progression or severity while steps and evidence are about disease risk (or the reverse), and steps carry no aspect field, so claims cannot reach the right aspect.

themes.name: mechanism_prose_beyond_citations
themes.description: Mechanism prose and notes assert facts (expression rankings, interactions, variant effects, cell types) that no cited text states, misread or overstate the cited text, or rely on citations given only in prose.

themes.name: disease_feature_as_cause
themes.description: Steps make a defining feature of the disease (intestinal inflammation, contractile dysfunction, glomerular injury, photoreceptor loss) or a near-synonym its cause, restating the definition rather than a mechanism.

themes.name: evidence_budget_unmet_or_padded
themes.description: Runs cite nothing or too little (budget minimums unmet without abstaining, specialists unused), or pad the source count with off-topic records.

themes.name: no_defect_confirmation
themes.description: Curator notes confirming correct behaviour (low confidence matching weak evidence, honest abstention on decoy genes) rather than a problem.

themes.name: other
themes.description: One-offs: source-record artefacts (ChEMBL mapping, preprint ids written as PMIDs), steps copied from paper titles, weak or secondary-only sources, text leaked from another gene's draft, and report counts that mix run gaps with BioLean gaps.

themes.name: database_record_cited_as_mechanism
themes.description: Records that cannot state a mechanistic step get cited as if they did: GWAS rows, Open Targets scores, ChEMBL rows, text-mined STRING edges, HPA/CELLxGENE expression, constraint scores, undirected MGI 'abnormal X' annotations, and circular enrichments run on the input gene set.

themes.name: cited_text_silent_on_step
themes.description: The cited paper or UniProt text never names the step's entities or the link (general reviews, papers about other genes, text read loosely), so the step has no support.

themes.name: strong_evidence_has_no_step
themes.description: The run's best evidence (variant-to-disease GWAS rows, direct gene-disease or C4-schizophrenia statements, available UniProt texts) states a link the chain never writes, often because the variant was dropped from the chain or a self-loop 'gene increases protein' was used instead, so it is cited at the wrong step, at no step, or not at all.

themes.name: allele_effect_on_gene_unstated
themes.description: Risk alleles carry an OR or beta, but nothing says whether the allele raises or lowers gene function (or whether a mouse allele is a null), so the gene-level sign rests on an assumption.

themes.name: unsigned_steps_block_routes
themes.description: Steps are associated_with/binds or have polarity 'unknown' even when notes, labels or the title state a direction, so no arm composes and the disease claims have no route.

themes.name: chain_not_connected
themes.description: Steps do not link object-to-subject: stars, fan-ins, parallel edges, restarts at the gene, mismatched near-identical nodes, or chains that are reversed or circular (disease as the first node).

themes.name: chain_omits_mechanism_or_disease
themes.description: The chain leaves out what the title or mechanism claims (named genes, intermediates, the titled process) or stops at a phenotype or expression site without reaching the disease.

themes.name: disease_feature_as_cause
themes.description: The last step links the disease to its own defining feature or restates a definition (glomerular inflammation, steatosis, ECM remodelling, excessive pruning), so it is a restatement, not a cause.

themes.name: internal_sign_contradiction
themes.description: A step's polarity, the mechanism, the title, or a sibling hypothesis disagree on direction (often the knockout's change encoded as the gene's effect), so arms compose to the opposite of the claim.

themes.name: counter_evidence_ignored
themes.description: contradicting_evidence is always empty: the run never looks for counter-evidence and ignores its own citations that refute or undercut its steps.

themes.name: mechanism_beyond_sources
themes.description: The mechanism or notes assert biology the sources do not support or that curated records contradict (shared promoters, functions inferred from domains, wrong binding partner such as IL23R-TYK2 skipping IL12RB1, causal claims from bare associations).

themes.name: confidence_support_overstated
themes.description: Confidence or support labels ('high', 'medium', 'grounded') do not match the evidence: few or no citations state any step, and none reaches the disease.

themes.name: uncited_or_empty_runs
themes.description: Runs or steps cite nothing (empty sources.json or specialist bundles), or quote figures without any accession, so no claim can be checked.

themes.name: budget_and_gene_coverage_unenforced
themes.description: Runs below the budget minimums (evidence, sources, hypotheses) are accepted without abstaining, and input genes are left unexplained or padded into hypotheses without a reason.

themes.name: grounding_and_typing_errors
themes.description: Nodes have empty or wrong CURIEs, wrong kinds, compound or class-level labels, misused relation types, or wrong or missing context (tissue, cell).

themes.name: abstention_unverifiable
themes.description: Abstentions cite pseudo-accessions (e.g. GWAS:X:no-association) that are not in sources.json, cite the wrong record type, overstate records, or decline genes for not fitting the main hypothesis.

themes.name: falsification_misdesigned
themes.description: Falsification tests are missing, test off-chain nodes or the wrong aspect, use an inconsistent 'expected' field, contradict the mechanism, cannot tell genes apart, or repeat experiments already reported.

themes.name: evidence_about_other_entity_or_context
themes.description: Cited evidence is about a different species (mouse, zebrafish, 'By similarity'), disease (parent pulmonary fibrosis, broader trait, pleiotropy), cell model, or gene (variant in a neighbouring gene, record for another gene), and the run does not flag it.

themes.name: curator_notes_not_defects
themes.description: These are positive or neutral curator notes, not defects: labels found honest, gene abstentions found honest, or a record of a curation decision such as a bridge not added.

themes.name: other
themes.description: One-offs: a correlational proxy study used for causal wording, risk-vs-severity aspect mismatches, a marker gene used as a cause, a hypothesis restating one paper, ambiguous or truncated source records, a missing composition rule for binds chains, notes not matching steps, and a citation used in conflicting roles.

themes.name: missing_ontology_term
themes.description: No ontology term exists for a process, state, phenotype or molecule class the run names, so the curator has to make a BLN term or ground to a broader parent term.

themes.name: variant_modelling
themes.description: Variants are modelled badly: there is no form for variant classes, haplotypes, allele dosage, an unreported allele or a protein-change-to-allele mapping, and no link (member-of-class, gain or loss of function) that lets variant-level association or knock-in evidence count for a gene-level effect step or claim.

themes.name: prefix_kind_and_corpus_defects
themes.description: Some corpus terms cannot be used or mislead: render.py gives no kind to NCIT, PW and ECOCORE-imported terms and maps all of SO to variant, and some corpus definitions or synonyms are wrong (GO:0140888 type II only, LOAD as a synonym of Alzheimer disease 2, HP:0004302 with no definition).

themes.name: phenotype_species_choice
themes.description: There is no rule for choosing HP, MP or UPHENO when a human-gene claim's phenotype comes from mouse data or HP lacks the term, and no form for an animal-model analogue phenotype, so the choice decides whether chains connect.

themes.name: evidence_taxon_and_design_fields
themes.description: An evidence row holds one kind and one taxon, with no primate, unknown or inferred taxon, no source species or paralogue for 'By similarity', and no way to record a span that mixes designs or does not say its design.

themes.name: evidence_kind_table_gaps
themes.description: The evidence-kind table has no row for Open Targets scores, HPA expression, immunostaining, Alliance disease-model records, STRING edges on non-binds statements, or Reactome/KEGG over-representation versus membership, so curators pick kinds inconsistently.

themes.name: kind_weight_miscalibration
themes.description: Kind weights ignore evidence strength and the taxon gap: one curatedDb row (STRING edge, UniProt line, MGI mouse annotation) or one review sentence makes a statement established, while large GWAS or primary experiments stay unsupported, and taxonConsistent false is flagged but not discounted.

themes.name: evidence_double_counting
themes.description: Nothing groups records that share one source (OT copies of UniProt text, OT scores built from the GWAS rows beside them, several MGI annotations from one paper, one citation counted under split statements), so one finding counts several times.

themes.name: null_signless_claims_and_verdicts
themes.description: Claims and arms cannot express nulls, absent associations, independence or an open net sign; unsigned hypotheses compose to nothing; null records are weighed like tested results; and the report hides borrowed routes, dropped disbelief and partial support.

themes.name: claim_level_evidence_slot
themes.description: Claims have no evidence slot, so supporting or contradicting texts about the gene-disease claim or an unstated premise have nowhere to attach when no step carries them, and are excluded or dropped.

themes.name: abstention_not_captured
themes.description: The format has no slot for a run's abstention, and sources.py does not fetch its citations, so abstentions cannot be curated or checked.

themes.name: pipeline_tool_gaps
themes.description: Tooling gaps in sources.py, render.py, terms.py and Lean: contradicting citations go unmarked, note fields are not rendered, evidence refs are not checked against citations, the checker does not match the guide, search misses synonyms, and distinctEvidence drops a refutation that shares a PMID.

themes.name: abnormal_x_and_mgi_rules
themes.description: The undirected-change and MGI 'abnormal X' rules are incomplete: they cover objects but not subjects, do not cover 'required for normal X', 'disrupted' or 'dysfunction', conflict over no_direction when the target is the abnormal-X phenotype, and leave allele type (null or conditional) to MGI nomenclature.

themes.name: sign_derivation_rules
themes.description: The guide lacks rules for getting a sign from wording or sources: low or high quality values, clearance objects, labels or qualifiers that imply a direction, participation or 'Involved in', inverting loss of function on objects, cited texts that disagree, and signs given only in falsification tests.

themes.name: disease_aspect_rules
themes.description: The risk, severity and progression aspect is unclear: where it comes from, how 'pathology' or 'modifier' maps to one, what to do with dual-aspect targets or disease features, and the fact that evidence carries no aspect, all of which decide whether routes compose.

themes.name: context_refinement_and_hierarchy
themes.description: Refinements and the ontology hierarchy do not compose: there is no lift from a refined node to its base, no is_a passage, no rule for evidence on a parent or narrower class or disease subtype, and no policy for structured or run-wide context fields.

themes.name: compound_labels_and_merges
themes.description: Multi-part, slash, disjunctive, gene-dependent and mediated labels, and set-valued subjects, must be split, merged or collapsed by curator judgement, and these merge or grain choices quietly decide which routes exist.

themes.name: relation_and_target_kinds
themes.description: Statement forms reject needed kinds: protein complexes, processes as amount targets, diseases as subjects, gene-gene associations, cellular-component targets, and localisation or translocation, which the relation table does not cover.

themes.name: interaction_and_qualifier_forms
themes.description: There is no form for effect modification, second-hit or genotype-conditional effects (condition refinements do not compose), set points, 'sustained' responses, metabolite pools, cargo-specific processes, or comorbidity.

themes.name: other
themes.description: One-offs: two parallel outcomes of one perturbation as evidence for a step, a citation listed as contradicting that actually supports, definitional readings for bridges, has_phenotype disease definitions as bridges, and positive confirmations.

themes.name: single_database_record_established
themes.description: One curatedDb record (a UniProt function line, or a STRING edge counted as curatedDb under the 0.15 channel cut even when text-mining or pathway co-membership drives it) alone reaches belief 0.8 and 'established'.

themes.name: evidence_kind_and_strength_gaps
themes.description: The evidence-kind table lacks rows or grades (case report, Mendelian segregation, enzymology, HPA, Open Targets aggregate scores, GO annotations in enrichment rows), and hedged, proxy or composed evidence enters at full weight for its kind.

themes.name: sign_from_wording_rules
themes.description: The guide signs an unknown-polarity leads_to step only from a cited text, which conflicts with its no_sign definition and with direction words in labels, notes or mechanisms; its loss-of-function word list and undirected-change rule leave out 'dysfunction', 'defect', undirected subjects and required_for on structures.

themes.name: claim_construction_rules
themes.description: The guide does not settle a claim's subject, aspect, number per gene, or end-node and phenotype claims when the title, mechanism and chain disagree, or when chains fork or start at a variant or the disease.

themes.name: binding_complex_and_interaction_forms
themes.description: Binding is a rel that never composes, and there is no node or form for protein complexes, gene pairs, joint causes, ordered cascades, conditional or two-sided effects, or one gene modifying another's effect.

themes.name: target_kind_gaps
themes.description: Effect targets cannot be a cellular component, cell type, organism population, splicing or isoform pattern, gene expression or a gene-specific process, and effect versus participation and process-versus-amount kinds are forced, so nodes get re-kinded or mis-stated.

themes.name: missing_terms_and_approx_grounding
themes.description: No ontology term exists for the node (or for a gene's unnamed variant class), or its prefix (NCIT, MPATH) is rejected by render.py, so curators use broader, mouse or BLN terms with no field marking the grounding as approximate.

themes.name: curated_json_missing_fields
themes.description: Unexpressed entries and exclusions lack fields: multiple categories, the citing step, grounded nodes, context, the reason a direction is none, a narrowing qualifier, overlapping-category precedence, title-only or wrong-gene categories, and the run's falsification tests.

themes.name: abstention_no_form
themes.description: A run's abstention or gene-level null result (genes, reason, cited evidence) has no place in curated.json, and sources.py does not fetch its records, so it cannot be checked or counted.

themes.name: variant_to_gene_link
themes.description: There is no variant-to-gene statement or gene-assignment field, so GWAS allele associations and their directions cannot carry to the gene, gene-level genetic support stays unsigned or is excluded, and the stronger leads_to wording earns less than associated_with.

themes.name: claim_level_evidence_no_home
themes.description: Evidence that bears on a hypothesis claim directly (GWAS rows, contradicting citations, chain shortcuts) cannot attach, because evidence attaches only to statements and bridges are allowed only to fill gaps.

themes.name: evidence_double_counting
themes.description: Evidence from overlapping samples or the same source is fused as independent, distinctEvidence drops a refuting item that shares a PMID with a supporting one, and split steps or shared flips inflate report counts.

themes.name: cross_species_and_paralogs
themes.description: Mouse or zebrafish evidence counts in full for human claims, and the taxon field cannot record orthology checks, paralog splits (C4A/C4B, meis1b) or the source species of crossSpecies text, while the taxon lint stays hidden.

themes.name: definitions_only_for_bridges
themes.description: Ontology definitions that state or sign a run step (GO, HP, MONDO) are allowed only in bridges, so they cannot be evidence on steps, and some corpus definitions (MONDO IgA nephropathy) are too thin to bridge.

themes.name: context_refinement_rule
themes.description: The guide does not say when a step's structured context (cell type, tissue, state) 'limits the result', and refining one step cuts the chain from its context-free neighbours.

themes.name: term_hierarchy_not_linked
themes.description: BioLean has no rule carrying evidence or links along term hierarchies (parent and child process, part-of, regulation-of-X and X, refinement and existing term, parent and subtype disease), so evidence at a different grain either fits loosely or fails to connect.

themes.name: unsigned_or_per_gene_claim_form
themes.description: Claims must be signed, and no_claim_reason applies to the whole hypothesis, so unsigned, association, either-or and chain-signed-only claims, and per-gene 'no claim' reasons, cannot be recorded.

themes.name: verdict_and_report_labels
themes.description: The verdict has nothing between 'unsupported' and 'established', and the report cannot tell a missing sign from a disconnected chain, or show a refutation on an arm.

themes.name: allele_direction_and_type_unstated
themes.description: Source records leave the allele's meaning unclear (GWAS risk allele versus beta direction, MGI or AGR allele type unstated), and the guide has no rule for reading a direction from them.

themes.name: tool_checks_and_fixed_bugs
themes.description: Gaps and bugs in sources.py, render.py and terms.py: missed searches, mechanism-only citations not fetched, a stale unsigned_association category still accepted, no wrong-gene check, one cited_as role per accession, uncited text accepted, and two already-fixed v1 bugs.

themes.name: other
themes.description: One-offs: disease-first associated_with steps reoriented with no rule, the 'translocates' relation missing from the relation table, and drug-target plus indication records that only state a link when joined.

themes.name: Chain does not reach the disease
themes.description: Steps do not join end to start, or the chain stops at a phenotype, skips the titled intermediates, or ends on a feature that defines the disease, so genes have no real route to the disease.
themes.fix: Validate that each step's object is the next step's subject, that the last node is the disease CURIE, and that the last step is not one of the disease's own defining features; reject chains that fail.
themes.example: IPF run: H1.1 ends at ER stress, H1.2 restarts at TOLLIP and H1.3 starts at 'proteotoxic stress', so TOLLIP has no route to IPF.

themes.name: Database records cited as causal steps
themes.description: GWAS rows, Open Targets scores, ChEMBL, MGI, HPA/CELLxGENE expression, STRING edges and enrichments on the input gene list are cited for directed mechanism steps they cannot state.
themes.fix: Tag every source with a record type and allow each type only on the step kinds it can state (for example gene-level records only on gene-to-disease steps, enrichment and expression never on causal steps).
themes.example: IgA nephropathy run: a Reactome 'Complement cascade' over-representation (2 of 163 entities) is cited as evidence that CFH inhibits complement.

themes.name: Cited text does not state the step
themes.description: Steps are uncited, or cite papers and UniProt entries that do not name the step's entities or state a weaker or different relation.
themes.fix: Require a verbatim quote span per step and check automatically that the quote is in the source and names both the subject and the object.
themes.example: Crohn run: PMID:36076306 is about stem cells primed with KYNA and IFN-gamma acting through IDO-1, not a kynurenic acid-GPR35 axis.

themes.name: Good evidence sits at no step
themes.description: Supporting citations are attached to no step, or to the wrong one, and the run's strongest stated link is often never made into a step.
themes.fix: Reject supporting citations that are not attached to a step, and when a source states a link between two run entities, offer that link as a step.
themes.example: IgA nephropathy run: rs6677604 and the Cfh-mutant glomerulonephritis annotation bear on CFH to disease, a link no step makes, so they support nothing.

themes.name: GWAS variant and allele handling
themes.description: GWAS rows lack a named risk allele, are mapped to one gene at multi-gene loci or for proxy traits, and no variant-to-gene step says whether the allele raises or lowers the gene.
themes.fix: Add a required variant-to-gene step type with risk allele, mapped-gene method (eQTL, coding, position) and effect direction, and allow GWAS rows only on that step and variant-to-disease.
themes.example: Schizophrenia run: a C4/MHC risk variant carries an OR, but nothing states whether the allele raises or lowers C4A, so the gene-level sign is assumed.

themes.name: Steps left unsigned
themes.description: Steps use polarity 'unknown', 'binds' or 'associated_with' even when the label, note or cited text gives a direction, so no route composes.
themes.fix: Make polarity a required field, allow 'unknown' only with a stated reason, and reject 'associated_with' inside causal chains.
themes.example: Schizophrenia run: 'Sensorimotor gating deficit associated with schizophrenia' has polarity 'unknown' though the label implies one, so H5 has no route.

themes.name: Signs unsupported or contradictory
themes.description: A step's sign is not supported by its source, or is opposite to its source, its own note, the mechanism or a sibling hypothesis, so the composed route contradicts the claim.
themes.fix: Compute the composed chain sign in the tool and reject hypotheses whose stated direction differs; require the sign to come from the step's quote.
themes.example: Knockout phenotypes encoded as the gene's own effect, so a loss-of-function step on a bare gene subject composes to the opposite of the mechanism.

themes.name: Counter-evidence missing or misfiled
themes.description: contradicting_evidence is empty or malformed, and the run ignores its own citations that refute its steps or files the same record both ways.
themes.fix: Run a counter-evidence search per step in the tool, check every contradicting accession resolves in sources.json, and reject a citation listed as both support and contradiction.
themes.example: Schizophrenia run: GWAS:C1QA:no-association is listed as supporting and also as contradicting H1.

themes.name: Confidence labels overstated
themes.description: Confidence 'high'/'medium' or support 'grounded' is given to hypotheses with broken chains and steps no source states.
themes.fix: Compute confidence and support from chain connectivity and the share of steps with a checked quote, instead of taking the model's label.
themes.example: Schizophrenia run: almost every entity has an empty CURIE, yet every hypothesis says support 'grounded'.

themes.name: Node grounding and typing errors
themes.description: Nodes have empty or malformed CURIEs, wrong kinds, compound or vague labels, misused relations, or boilerplate contexts.
themes.fix: Ground every node through an ontology lookup that sets the CURIE and kind, and reject empty, malformed or compound nodes.
themes.example: Alzheimer's run: every node has an empty CURIE except the disease, written as the malformed 'EFO:MONDO_0004975'.

themes.name: Mechanism prose beyond the sources
themes.description: Mechanism text and notes assert facts no cited text states, misread a source, or use the wrong entity or accession.
themes.fix: Generate the mechanism text from the chain steps, or require each prose sentence to point to a step and its quote.
themes.example: Mechanism prose gives IL23R signalling straight through TYK2, skipping IL12RB1, which no cited record supports.

themes.name: Evidence from the wrong context
themes.description: Cited evidence is from another species, cell type, disease, gene or aspect (risk versus progression) than the step claims, and the run does not flag it.
themes.fix: Add required species, tissue, disease and aspect fields per step and compare them with the source's metadata, flagging mismatches.
themes.example: Schizophrenia run: H2.2's object is first-episode psychosis, broader than schizophrenia (66 of 113 later diagnosed).

themes.name: Falsification tests misdesigned or not new
themes.description: Falsification tests are unstructured, target off-chain nodes or the wrong aspect, conflict with the chain's sign, or restate an experiment already published.
themes.fix: Make the falsification test point to a chain step id with an expected direction taken from that step's sign, and check it against retrieved paper titles for novelty.
themes.example: A hypothesis and its falsification test restate a retrieved paper's title and its already-reported experiment.

themes.name: Gene coverage, budget and abstentions unchecked
themes.description: Input genes are left out or only named in titles, runs under the evidence or hypothesis budget are accepted, and abstentions cite records not in sources.json.
themes.fix: At the end of a run, check every input gene is in a step or a valid abstention, check abstention accessions resolve in sources.json, and fail runs below budget.
themes.example: Alzheimer's run: H3 cites 'GWAS:LPIN2:no-association' and H2 'AGR:MGI:1913860:no-phenotypes', neither in sources.json, so neither can be checked.

themes.name: One-offs and non-defects
themes.description: Source-record artefacts (preprint ids written as PMIDs, ChEMBL mapping), leaked text and other one-offs, plus curator notes that confirm correct behaviour.
themes.fix: Normalise source ids at fetch time, and keep positive curator notes out of the defect findings by giving them their own category.
themes.example: Curator note that a low-confidence label matched weak evidence, or that abstention on decoy genes was honest.

themes.name: Missing terms and approximate grounding
themes.description: No ontology term exists for many nodes, and some corpus prefixes (NCIT, PW, MPATH, ECOCORE) get no kind in render.py, so curators make BLN terms or ground to a broader parent and nothing records that it is approximate.
themes.fix: Give render.py kinds for NCIT, PW, MPATH and ECOCORE terms, split the SO mapping by term type, fix the bad corpus entries, and add a grounding field (exact, broader, BLN) on each node.
themes.example: 'Tissue damage' has NCIT:C50773 and MPATH:1 in the corpus, but render.py accepts neither prefix, so the node is left ungroundable.

themes.name: Variants and the variant-to-gene link
themes.description: There is no form for variant classes, haplotypes, dosage or allele type, and no variant-to-gene link, so GWAS and knock-in evidence and its direction cannot carry to a gene-level step or claim.
themes.fix: Add a variant node type (allele, haplotype, class, copy number) with a gene field and a declared effect (gain, loss, risk allele), plus a member-of or acts-through link that composes into gene-level routes.
themes.example: The APOE e4 allele is a two-SNP haplotype with no dbSNP ID, so it is recorded as one BLN variant and loses that it is a pair.

themes.name: Taxon, species and study design on evidence
themes.description: An evidence row holds one kind and one taxon, cannot record orthology, paralogues, source species or a mixed design, and there is no rule for HP versus MP when phenotype data come from mouse.
themes.fix: Make taxon a structured field (source species, ortholog or paralogue mapping, unknown or inferred), allow a list of designs per span, and add a phenotype-species rule enforced by the checker.
themes.example: One mouse C4 result supports both human C4A and C4B statements, and the taxon flag cannot say the mouse gene is the ortholog of both, so the same quote counts twice.

themes.name: Evidence-kind table gaps
themes.description: The kind table has no row for Open Targets scores, HPA expression, immunostaining, Alliance models, case reports, segregation, enzymology or pathway over-representation, so curators pick kinds inconsistently.
themes.fix: Add those rows to the kind table in code, with a hedged or proxy modifier that lowers weight, and have the checker reject sources whose type has no row.
themes.example: Open Targets association scores have no row; recorded as curatedDb on a first pass, one OT score alone made 'FAM13A goes with IPF' established.

themes.name: Kind weights ignore strength
themes.description: Weights depend only on kind, so one curatedDb row (UniProt line, STRING edge) reaches 'established' while huge GWAS or primary experiments stay unsupported, and the taxon flag is shown but not discounted.
themes.fix: Weight evidence by strength (sample size, p-value, STRING channel that drives the score), cap a single database record below the established threshold, and apply the taxon discount in the fusion.
themes.example: STRING C3-ARMS2 counts as curatedDb because its experimental channel (0.24) clears 0.15, though text-mining (0.62) supplies most of the 0.70 score, and it reaches belief 0.8.

themes.name: Double counting of shared sources
themes.description: Nothing groups records that share one source, so OT copies of UniProt text, OT scores built from adjacent GWAS rows, or several MGI rows from one paper fuse as independent, while distinctEvidence drops a refutation sharing a PMID.
themes.fix: Add a provenance or source-group key to evidence, fuse within a group once, and make distinctEvidence key on (source, polarity) rather than source alone.
themes.example: distinctEvidence keeps one item per PMID regardless of polarity, so S5's refuting Q8IV20 span is dropped and S5 fuses to b=4/5, d=0.

themes.name: Unsigned, null and per-gene claims and verdicts
themes.description: Claims must be signed, nulls and absent associations have no form, unsigned hypotheses compose to nothing, and the verdict has nothing between 'unsupported' and 'established' nor shows borrowed routes, refutations or a missing sign.
themes.fix: Allow unsigned and null claims and statements, weigh null records separately, allow per-gene no-claim reasons, and add verdict labels (partial, refuted, unsigned, disconnected) to the report.
themes.example: An MGI 'no abnormal phenotype detected' record (MP:0002169) is a null with no named phenotype and cannot refute a specific phenotype step.

themes.name: Claim-level evidence and bridges
themes.description: Evidence attaches only to statements and bridges only fill gaps, so texts that bear on the gene-disease claim directly, or ontology definitions that state a step, have no home and are dropped.
themes.fix: Add an evidence slot on claims (supports or refutes) and let definitions be a 'definitional' evidence kind on steps, separate from bridges.
themes.example: PMID:42601455 (PLCG2 loss-of-function variants raise AD risk tenfold) has nowhere to go because no step states it and a bridge equal to the whole claim is not a bridge.

themes.name: Abstentions and missing curated.json fields
themes.description: curated.json has no slot for a run's abstention or gene-level null, and unexpressed entries lack fields such as citing step, category list, reason for no direction and falsification tests; sources.py does not fetch abstention citations.
themes.fix: Add an abstention block (genes, reason, cited accessions) and the missing exclusion fields to the curated.json schema, and make sources.py fetch every accession the run cites anywhere.
themes.example: The run abstains on RBM27 and SMIM32 citing six accessions (GWAS no-association, HPA, AGR) that are not in sources.json, so the abstention cannot be checked.

themes.name: Pipeline tool gaps
themes.description: sources.py, render.py, terms.py and the Lean checker have gaps: one cited_as role per accession, contradicting prose citations unmarked, notes not rendered, refs not checked against citations, synonym search misses, and a stale category still accepted.
themes.fix: Let sources.py store a list of cited_as roles and parse contradicting_evidence, check every evidence ref against the run's citations, render notes, search synonyms in terms.py, and drop unsigned_association.
themes.example: sources.json gives OT:NXPH3 only the 'chain' role though run.json also lists it in H3's contradicting_evidence.

themes.name: Sign rules from wording and sources
themes.description: The guide's sign rules conflict and are incomplete: no_sign versus direction words in labels, 'abnormal X' and 'dysregulates' rules, subjects, 'required for', 'dysfunction', 'defect', quality objects, and MGI allele types.
themes.fix: Encode the sign rules as one ordered table in the checker, with an explicit precedence and full loss-of-function word list, and require an allele-type field on model-organism evidence.
themes.example: 'LIPC leads_to lipid metabolism dysregulation (unknown)' matches both the unknown-polarity no_sign rule and the 'dysregulates X gives effect pos on abnormal-X' rule.

themes.name: Claim construction and disease aspect
themes.description: The guide does not settle a claim's subject, aspect, number per gene or end node when title, mechanism and chain disagree, and evidence carries no aspect, yet the aspect decides whether routes compose.
themes.fix: Derive claim subject, sign and aspect from the chain in code with a checked override field, and add an aspect field to evidence so routes compose only across matching aspects.
themes.example: 'Exacerbating IgA glomerulonephritis' fits both severity and progression in the aspect table; the curator chose severity and the audit chose progression.

themes.name: Context, hierarchy and node grain
themes.description: Refined nodes do not lift to their base, there is no is_a or part_of passage, no rule for evidence at a parent or subtype grain, and split or merge choices for compound labels quietly decide which routes exist.
themes.fix: Let composition follow refinement-to-base and is_a or part_of links with a discount, and record each split or merge as an explicit node mapping the report shows.
themes.example: H1's only composed arm (INPP5D to Abeta clearance to AD) depends on merging 'plaque clearance' and 'microglial amyloid-beta clearance' as GO:0097242, borrowing H5.3.

themes.name: Relation and target kinds
themes.description: Statement forms reject needed kinds (cellular components, cell types, splicing, gene expression, diseases as subjects, gene-gene associations, translocation), so nodes get re-kinded or the step is mis-stated.
themes.fix: Widen the allowed subject and target kinds per relation and add the missing relations (translocates, located-in) to the relation table in code.
themes.example: An associated_with step whose object is a cellular component has no assoc target, so it becomes a rel RO:0001025 (located in), which the relation table does not list.

themes.name: Binding, complexes and interactions
themes.description: Binding is a rel that never composes, and there is no form for protein complexes, joint causes, effect modification, genotype-conditional effects, set points or comorbidity.
themes.fix: Add a complex node with member genes, let binds compose when a cited text gives a direction, and add a modifier or conditional-effect statement form.
themes.example: IL12B acts through the IL-23 heterodimer binding IL12RB1 and IL23R; with no complex node it was recorded as IL12B interacting with IL23R.
